question.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=6 \\ -{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-2 \\ {y}_{1}-{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =6, \\ {y}_{2} & =-2+{y}_{1} \\  & =-2+6 \\  & =4, \\ {y}_{3} & =-{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\  & =-(6)+4 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
